clue.text: Run on fresh paper

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: fresh means new
to run fast is to sprint

explanation.surface: An instruction to print again on clean sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsprint is the cheap paper on which newspapers are printed.

clue.text: More drink given to baby

parts.note: a pup is a baby dog or seal

explanation.surface: Someone gives an infant another bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-up is a refill of a glass, an extra serving of drink.

clue.text: I've murdered many: or haven't I?

parts.note: the solution read as an instruction says to take seven letters and mix them terribly, and those seven letters, rearranged, spell these words

explanation.surface: A killer boasts of a huge body count, then has second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first two words of the answer as fodder and the last as an anagram signal: IVANTHE made terrible gives HAVENTI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian tsar Ivan IV was notorious for his massacres and killings.

clue.text: Loathing the crown, for example, cardinal

parts.note: a crown is one example of headwear
cardinal is a deep scarlet colour

explanation.surface: A republican cardinal hates the monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing and hatred are synonyms for intense dislike.

clue.text: Old reform movement, it takes reformist leader back into the breach

indicators.note: into says the reversed pieces are put inside the gap

parts.note: a chasm is a gap or breach

indicators.note: back says the pair of pieces before it is read in reverse order
leader picks the opening letter of the word reformist

explanation.surface: A historical reform group lets a radical leader back into the gap.
explanation.walkthrough: IT plus R makes ITR, and 'back' turns it to RTI, which goes into CHASM.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartism was a nineteenth-century British working-class campaign for political reform.

clue.text: Unfit — that is describing being ill, out of shape

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing round means one piece goes around another
out of shape says the letters of the words before it are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone sick and unfit is declared unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' looks like 'portraying' but here means drawing round; 'out of shape' is the anagram signal for the two words that follow 'describing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineligible means not qualified or not fit to be chosen.

clue.text: Fee reduced by a third for this club?

definitions.text: Fee reduced by a third for this club?

parts.words: Fee reduced by a third for this club?
parts.note: drop one of the three letters of the word fee and you get the chemical symbol for a metal, which also names a golf club

explanation.surface: A golf club discounts its membership fee.
explanation.walkthrough: Fe is the chemical symbol for the metal; the golf club of the same name has a metal head.
explanation.definitionFit: Fe is the chemical symbol of this metal, and it is also a type of golf club.

clue.text: Painful area on skin in ear

definitions.meaning: a hard painful patch of skin, usually on the foot
the cereal grain grows in an ear on the stalk

explanation.definitionFit: Corn is both a painful callus on the foot and the grain borne in ears.

clue.text: Hot in breeze, then suffering with a fur coat

indicators.note: then says the next pieces follow on
in says the letter goes inside the easy thing

parts.note: a breeze is something easy, a cinch
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
suffering means ill

explanation.surface: Someone shivering in a breeze, then ill, wraps up in fur.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinchilla is the soft grey fur of a small Andean rodent, prized for coats.

clue.text: In audition, scent struggle — that's the spirit!

indicators.note: in audition means as heard by a listener, so the words are spoken

parts.note: a scent is an odour; to vie is to compete or struggle

explanation.surface: A perfume contest is toasted with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic British accent, 'odour vie' sounds like the French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de vie is a clear fruit brandy, a strong spirit.

clue.text: In a couple of rounds, score with exchange of passes

indicators.note: In says the following pieces sit inside the two letters

parts.note: a round is the letter O, so two of them
to score a goal is to net

explanation.surface: A boxer scores in two rounds; footballers trade passes.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-two in football is a quick pass and return between two players.

clue.text: Yet more spring, I fancy for flowering plant

parts.note: yet as in yet more means even, as in even more

indicators.note: fancy as a verb used loosely here signals rearranging the letters before it

explanation.surface: A gardener longs for more springtime blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges MORE SPRING I into INGPRIMROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening primrose is a yellow-flowered plant whose blooms open at dusk.

clue.text: Cross in match ending in penalty

parts.note: a test is an international cricket or rugby match

indicators.note: ending in picks the final letter of the word penalty

explanation.surface: A player gets angry when a game ends with a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Testy and cross both mean irritable.

clue.text: Muse sincere, I'm false

indicators.note: false says the letters of the words before it are not in their true order

explanation.surface: Someone thinks aloud about being insincere.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse on the past is to reminisce, to recall memories.

clue.text: Hear no sound from charger

indicators.note: Hear tells the solver to listen to the word rather than read it

parts.note: nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: A horse is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A neigh is the cry of a horse, and a charger is a warhorse.

clue.text: Feeble person controlling planet, then stimulating types take the lead

indicators.note: then says the last piece follows
controlling as holding something in check means one piece wraps another

parts.note: a wet is a feeble, ineffectual person
Earth is a planet
rousers are people who stir others up

explanation.surface: A weakling runs the world, then agitators seize power.
explanation.walkthrough: WET is British slang for a feeble person.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear the trousers is the idiom for being the dominant partner, being in charge.

clue.text: Hopeless route to mention, northbound

parts.note: a path is a route

indicators.note: in a down clue northbound means the word is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: to cite is to mention

explanation.surface: A lost traveller describes a road heading north.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic means feeble or hopeless, as in a pathetic effort.

clue.text: Design inside amazing houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the letters sit within the two words

explanation.surface: An interior designer's work is admired.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a plan or design in the mind.

clue.text: In character, girl and I do as we're told?

indicators.note: In says the following pieces go inside

parts.note: tone is character, as in the tone of a place
Ethel is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Two well-behaved children play obedient characters.
explanation.definitionFit: To toe the line is the idiom for obeying the rules.

clue.text: Matador sees every finish of bullfight? So far one or two

indicators.note: every finish of picks the last letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: A bullfighter has fought only a couple of bulls so far.
explanation.definitionFit: Torero is the Spanish word for a bullfighter, matador being one kind.

clue.text: Books to include Orwell, only every second in promotion

indicators.note: to include says the large piece takes the small one inside it

parts.note: books are publications

indicators.note: only every second takes the second, fourth and sixth letters of the name

explanation.surface: A publisher's catalogue is boosted by Orwell's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Public relations is the work of promoting an organisation's image.

clue.text: Was aware more grumbling out loud could lead to complaint

indicators.note: out loud tells the solver to hear the words spoken

parts.note: to be aware is to know, so knew; moanier means more given to moaning

explanation.surface: Someone realised grumbling would only make matters worse.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an illness, and pneumonia is a lung infection.

clue.text: This digital in code? Not quite!

definitions.text: This digital in code? Not quite!

parts.words: This digital in code? Not quite!
parts.note: digital points to a finger-shaped item and code cut short is cod, so think of a breaded finger of cod

explanation.surface: A cipher puzzle about digital code.
explanation.walkthrough: Fish fingers are a British freezer staple: breaded sticks of white fish such as cod.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish fingers are finger-shaped breaded pieces often made from cod.

clue.text: Step up in career ultimately welcomed by setter

indicators.note: welcomed by says the letter is taken inside the other piece

parts.note: cement is something that sets

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word career

explanation.surface: A crossword setter takes a promotion late in their career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler (usually ME) but is cement, something that sets.
explanation.definitionFit: An increment is a step up, such as a rise on a pay scale.

clue.text: Cricket ball hit a player

parts.note: to chin someone is to punch them on the chin
a man is a player in a team or a piece in chess

explanation.surface: A fielder is struck by a cricket ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the term names a left-arm wrist-spinner's delivery that turns into a right-handed batter.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this is the old name for a left-arm unorthodox spin delivery.

clue.text: Truth so encapsulates it

indicators.note: encapsulates means encloses, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: so as in so good means very

explanation.surface: A short statement captures the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Verity is a formal word for truth.

clue.text: Very large gong, southern Eritrean origins

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or honour, such as the OBE

indicators.note: origins picks the opening letter of the word Eritrean

explanation.surface: A huge gong comes from southern Eritrea.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means grossly overweight, very large in body.

clue.text: Short play shortened

indicators.note: shortened means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a drama is a play

explanation.surface: A brief play is cut further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like an adjective but is a British pub term for a measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A short is a small measure of spirits, such as a dram of whisky.
